## 03d36f36821e

**Status: reproduced teaching defect; target left unchanged.** Generator SHA-256: `74c38e453bed52bafc5200e61c931fbaae6b67fc6dc41f92256fb0cf55abf5a0`. Executed rule hash: `7aff92e10cd5`.

The intended rule selects the component with the most enclosed zero **regions**. A plausible rival selects the component with the most enclosed zero **cells**. Because component textures are drawn independently and there is no lesson/rival contract, three consecutive demonstrations often fail to separate those hypotheses.

Across exactly 31,500 overlapping three-demo-plus-query windows—bands easy/medium/hard; seeds 0–499; generated sample indices 0–23, yielding 21 starts per seed—the rival fit all three demonstrations but disagreed on the query in **3,246/31,500 (10.3048%)** windows. Counts by band were 1,113/10,500 easy, 1,075/10,500 medium, and 1,058/10,500 hard.

Exact source-bound counterexample: difficulty `easy`, seed `0`, demonstrations at sample indices `13,14,15`, query at `16`. All four inputs were generated by the audited source and passed its validator. The supported Racket outputs agree with the “most enclosed cells” rival for all three demonstrations and disagree on the query. Evidence: `checks/audit/03d36f36821e/verified.json`, `checks/audit/03d36f36821e/inputs.json`, `checks/audit/03d36f36821e/rival_outputs.json`, `checks/audit/03d36f36821e/racket.json`, and `checks/audit/03d36f36821e/hole_cell_rival_probe.json`.

This is a finite rival result, not proof that 10.3048% of all possible lessons are ambiguous. It demonstrates a reproducible, reference-lawful shortcut under the generator’s actual consecutive three-demo assembly.
